validation.notes: Lotes 1–2 curated for Teacher Israel Ventura class guided practice and future mocks. Original workplace English only (not ETS material). Lote 2 added ad + article genres.

text.content:
Dear Ms. Patel,

Thank you for joining yesterday’s online demonstration of our inventory software. We were pleased to answer your questions about reporting tools and user permissions.
As discussed, I have attached a [[131]] proposal that outlines pricing for a 25-user license. The quote remains valid for 30 days from the date of this message.
Our implementation team can schedule a kickoff meeting as early as next week. [[132]], we recommend completing the order form by Friday if you would like the May installation window.

Please let me know if you need a live trial for two additional managers. [[133]]

I look forward to your [[134]].

Best regards,
Marcus Chen
Account Manager, StockFlow Systems

questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun "proposal." "Detailed" correctly modifies the noun.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the noun "detail" or "details" when an adjective slot is required.

questions.explanation: The second sentence is a logical result of wanting the May window: act by Friday. "Therefore" marks consequence.
questions.commonMistake: Using "In contrast" when there is no opposing idea.

text.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All employees
From: Facilities Management
Date: March 12
Subject: Temporary changes to visitor parking

Beginning Monday, the north lot will be closed for resurfacing. Visitors should use the south lot and display a guest pass on the dashboard. Guest passes are [[135]] at the security desk in Building A.
Construction vehicles will enter through Gate 2 only. [[136]], employees are asked not to leave personal vehicles overnight in the south lot during the project.

We appreciate your [[137]] while the work is completed. [[138]]

Please contact Facilities at ext. 4400 with questions.

questions.explanation: Passes can be obtained at the desk — "available" means ready to be used or obtained.
questions.commonMistake: Selecting a similar adjective (affordable / admirable) that does not fit "at the security desk."

questions.explanation: The sentence adds another restriction related to the parking project. "In addition" is the additive connector.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "Instead," which would replace an idea rather than add one.

questions.explanation: After the possessive determiner "your," a noun is required. "Patience" is the noun form.
questions.commonMistake: Using the adjective "patient" after "your," where a noun slot is needed.

text.content:
NOTICE

Network Maintenance — Sunday, April 6

The Information Technology department will perform essential upgrades to the company network this Sunday from 1:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. During this period, email and shared drives will be [[139]] unavailable.

Please save open files and log out of all systems before you leave on Friday. [[140]], remote access will also be interrupted, so plan offline work if you expect to work from home early Sunday morning.

Most services should be [[141]] by 5:30 a.m. [[142]]

For urgent issues after the window, contact the on-call technician at 555-0188.
— IT Operations

questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the adjective "unavailable." "Temporarily" is the adverb form.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the adjective "temporary" to modify another adjective.

questions.explanation: The sentence adds another impact of the outage (remote access). "Furthermore" is additive.
questions.commonMistake: Using "Otherwise," which signals an alternative consequence, not an added fact.

questions.explanation: After maintenance, services are brought back — "restored" means returned to normal operation.
questions.commonMistake: Picking a look-alike verb (reserved / restrained) that does not mean "back online."

text.content:
Dear Mr. Alvarez,

We are delighted to offer you a summer internship in the Marketing Department at BrightHarbor Media. Your start date will be June 2, and the internship will last ten weeks.
During the program, you will assist with social media campaigns and prepare [[143]] reports for weekly team meetings. You will also shadow a senior coordinator on client calls.
The position is paid at the rate listed in the enclosed agreement. [[144]], the company will provide a transit subsidy for commuting days spent at the downtown office.

Please sign and return the agreement by April 20 to [[145]] your place in the cohort. [[146]]

We look forward to welcoming you in June.

Sincerely,
Dana Whitfield
Human Resources Manager

questions.explanation: A noun is needed to modify "reports" in the compound sense "summary reports" (or act as the adjective-noun pattern). "Summary" is the correct form before "reports."
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the verb "summarize" where a noun modifier is required.

questions.explanation: The transit subsidy is an extra benefit beyond the pay rate. "In addition" signals that additive relationship.
questions.commonMistake: Using a contrast connector (Even so / By contrast) when the letter is listing benefits.

questions.explanation: Returning the signed agreement "confirms" (secures / verifies) the internship place.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing similar verbs: confine (restrict), conform (comply), confer (discuss/grant).

text.content:
ADVERTISEMENT

Upgrade Your Workspace with ErgoLift Pro
ErgoLift Pro is a height-adjustable desk designed for busy professionals. With a quiet motor and three memory presets, you can switch between sitting and standing [[147]].
Through September 30, corporate buyers receive 15% off orders of five or more units. [[148]], free delivery is included for offices within 50 miles of our warehouse.

Visit www.ergolift-pro.example to request a [[149]] quote for your team. [[150]]

ErgoLift — furniture that works as hard as you do.

questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb phrase "switch between sitting and standing." "Easily" is the adverb form.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the adjective "easy" to modify a verb.

questions.explanation: Free delivery is another benefit stacked on the discount. "In addition" marks that additive relationship.
questions.commonMistake: Using a contrast connector (Nevertheless / On the contrary) when the ad is listing extra perks.

questions.explanation: A quote tailored to a team's size and options is "customized" — made for a specific buyer.
questions.commonMistake: Selecting a look-alike adjective (customary / curious) that does not mean tailored pricing.

text.content:
NORTHBRIDGE TODAY — Staff Magazine

Cutting Packaging Waste at the Distribution Center

Last quarter, Northbridge Logistics launched a pilot program to reduce cardboard waste at its Riverside distribution center. Teams replaced oversized boxes with right-sized packaging and introduced reusable plastic totes for local deliveries.
Early results have been [[151]]. Material costs fell by nearly 12%, and fewer damaged shipments were reported. [[152]], drivers noted that the lighter totes were easier to load.

Managers plan a [[153]] rollout to two additional centers in January. [[154]]

Employees with suggestions may email greenops@northbridge.example.

questions.explanation: Context (cost savings and fewer damaged shipments) shows positive results. "Encouraging" means promising or favorable.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "discouraging," the opposite sense, or another adjective that does not fit the positive data.

questions.explanation: The drivers' comment adds another positive outcome. "Moreover" is the additive discourse marker.
questions.commonMistake: Using "In contrast" when the sentence continues the good-news pattern rather than opposing it.

questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun "rollout." "Gradual" correctly modifies "rollout."
questions.commonMistake: Choosing the adverb "gradually" where an adjective slot before a noun is required.

text.content:
Dear Mr. Okonkwo,

Thank you for contacting Apex Home Goods about order #AH-44921. We apologize for the delay in delivering your kitchen appliance set.
Our records show that the package left the warehouse on time. [[155]], a regional carrier backlog held the shipment at a sorting facility for three extra days.
The items are now out for delivery and should arrive by tomorrow evening. As a courtesy, we have applied a 10% [[156]] to your account for use on a future purchase.

Please accept our [[157]] for the inconvenience. [[158]]

Sincerely,
Priya Nair
Customer Care Specialist
Apex Home Goods

questions.explanation: The carrier backlog is bad news after saying the package left on time. "Unfortunately" signals that disappointing turn.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "Similarly" or "For instance," which do not mark an adverse development.

questions.explanation: In customer service, a store "credit" is money or value applied to an account for a future purchase.
questions.commonMistake: Picking a similar-looking noun (credential / critique) that does not mean account credit.

questions.explanation: After the possessive "our," a noun is required. "Apology" is the noun form in "accept our apology."
questions.commonMistake: Using the verb "apologize" after "our," where a noun is needed.

text.content:
MEMORANDUM

To: All department managers
From: Finance Department
Date: September 8
Subject: Revised policy for travel expense reimbursement

Effective October 1, employees must submit travel expense reports within ten business days of returning from a trip. Reports filed after that window will require director-level [[159]] before payment can be processed.
Itemized receipts remain mandatory for lodging, airfare, and meals above $25. [[160]], mileage claims must use the rate published on the intranet; handwritten estimates will no longer be accepted.

Please share this update with your teams and [[161]] that staff complete the short policy quiz by September 25. [[162]]

Questions may be directed to finance-help@firm.example.
— Controllers Office

questions.explanation: Late reports need director-level "approval" (authorization) before Finance pays them.
questions.commonMistake: Confusing similar nouns (approach / appearance) that do not mean authorization to pay.

questions.explanation: The mileage rule is an additional requirement alongside itemized receipts. "Furthermore" adds that policy point.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing "Conversely," which would introduce an opposite idea rather than another rule.

questions.explanation: Parallel to "share," the base-form verb "ensure" is needed after "Please … and."
questions.commonMistake: Using "ensuring" (gerund/participle) where a parallel imperative verb is required.
